podcast.title: Opening Act for The Beatles (1964)
podcast.body: Bill Black's Combo served as an opening act for The Beatles' concert at Maple Leaf Gardens in Toronto on September 6, 1964. However, like the other supporting acts, they were met with boos from the impatient crowd, who were exclusively eager to see The Beatles perform. "As the opening bands, which included Bill Black's combo...hit the stage to crowd-bood, they only wanted one band, and one band only."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Instrumental Hits and Opening for The Beatles (1960s)
podcast.body: Formed by Bill Black after his permanent departure from Elvis's band, Bill Black's Combo achieved a series of instrumental hits over several years, including eight Top 40 singles. Their popularity earned them the prestigious role of opening act for The Beatles' first US tour. "Bill Black's combo had eight top 40 hits, and were popular enough that they became the opening act for the Beatles' first US tour."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

concerts.title: The Beatles' first US tour (opening act)

xref.title: Opening Acts Booed by Impatient Crowd (1964)
xref.body: At the Maple Leaf Gardens concert in Toronto on September 6, 1964, the opening bands, which included Bill Black's Combo, The Exciters, Clarence "Frogman" Henry, and Jackie De Shannon, were met with boos from the crowd. The audience was impatient and made it clear they wanted only one band: The Beatles. "As the opening bands, which included Bill Black's combo, the exciders Clarence Frogman Henry, and the Celterie Jackie De Shannon hit the stage to crowd-bood, they only wanted one band, and one band only."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
